title: feat: one dev project for issues, pull requests and app submissions
author: ElliotEtag
pr_body_excerpt:
Follow-up to #15335. Dev becomes the single project for team work; its views separate the item types (`LIST ALL`, `PR`, `QUESTS`, `APPS`, `TRACKING`). Support stays for external issues.

- Every PR goes to Dev when it opens, so the `PR` view lists all open PRs
- App submissions and app-catalog PRs go to Dev instead of the Apps project. App review runs on the `APP-*` labels only, so nothing else depended on Apps; the Apps project is being closed (not deleted)
- Issues the classifier thinks are app submissions but lack `APP-SUBMISSION` also go to Dev, unlabelled, so a person confirms before the app review starts

gist.headline: One garden for the work
gist.blurb: The Dev project is now the hive’s single workbench for pull requests, app submissions, and team-tracked issues. Different views keep the pollen sorted; humans still get the final say on unlabelled app submissions.
gist.summary: GitHub project automation now routes every newly opened PR, app submission, app-catalog PR, and unlabelled suspected app-submission issue into the Dev project, whose views separate PRs, quests, apps, tracking, and all work.
gist.impact: Contributors and maintainers get one Dev project for open PR and app-review triage, while suspected submissions without APP-SUBMISSION wait for a human confirmation before review begins.
gist.visual_concept: Depict Dev as a cozy central garden workbench with separate labeled trays for PRs, quests, apps, and tracking; Polli acts as a calm organizer, moving paper cards into the right trays while one unlabelled app card waits under a small human-check stamp. Include code-plants and the retired Apps garden sign gently resting nearby to show consolidation rather than deletion.
gist.image_prompt: A cozy pixel art garden workbench labeled "DEV" has tidy little trays marked "PR", "QUESTS", "APPS", and "TRACKING", while Polli—the cute yellow-and-brown striped bee with light blue wings, pink cheek blush, a happy smile, and a tiny librarian scarf—sorts pull-request cards beside sprouting code-plants; one unlabelled app card waits under a small "CHECK" stamp, and a softly glowing retired "APPS" sign rests nearby. Cozy 8-bit pixel art aesthetic, soft lime green (#ecf874) and pastel gradient background, chunky retro sprites, warm lighting, lo-fi vibes like Stardew Valley or A Short Hike, nostalgic but beautiful.
